given_when_then.given: A Store Partner updates the quantity of a perishable SKU in their Real-Time Inventory Snapshot
given_when_then.when: The Order Allocation Engine attempts to allocate an Order Request for that SKU
given_when_then.then: The system shall reflect the updated quantity immediately and allow allocation only if stock is sufficient

given_when_then.given: An Order Request has successfully locked stock for a perishable item
given_when_then.when: The Customer cancels the Order Request before the fulfillment task begins
given_when_then.then: The system shall release the locked stock quantity back to the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot for other orders

given_when_then.given: Multiple Order Requests are attempting to allocate stock for the same perishable item simultaneously
given_when_then.when: The Order Allocation Engine processes the allocation requests
given_when_then.then: The system shall lock the available stock quantity to the first successful request and reject subsequent requests for that quantity to prevent overselling

given_when_then.given: An Order Request has locked stock but remains unconfirmed
given_when_then.when: The allocated time window expires without confirmation
given_when_then.then: The system shall automatically release the locked stock quantity back to the Real-Time Inventory Snapshot

success_criteria: The stock quantity associated with an Order Request is locked exclusively to that specific request immediately upon allocation.
Concurrent allocation attempts for the same SKU result in only one successful lock, with other attempts failing.
The system prevents overselling by ensuring available stock is not double-allocated to different Order Requests.
Locked stock is automatically released when the Order Request is cancelled or when the confirmation time window expires.
